name: Congenital Thyroid Malformation Without Hypothyroidism

criteria.description: Presence of congenital anatomical malformation of the thyroid gland confirmed by imaging
Normal thyroid hormone levels without clinical or biochemical hypothyroidism
Exclusion of acquired thyroid disorders or hypothyroid conditions
Supportive genetic testing showing mutations associated with thyroid dysgenesis without hypothyroidism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital thyroid anatomical malformation with normal thyroid function tests and exclusion of acquired thyroid disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and thyroid function tests in the neonatal period or early infancy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital thyroid gland hypoplasia or agenesis without hypothyroidism
searchTerms: underdeveloped or missing thyroid at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ectopic thyroid tissue detected by imaging

common.symptomName: Normal thyroid hormone levels despite gland malformation
searchTerms: normal thyroid hormone despite gland issues

common.symptomName: Neck asymmetry or palpable thyroid abnormality
Mild dysphonia or hoarseness due to anatomical variation

occasional.symptomName: Mild dysphagia related to thyroid anatomical anomaly
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to thyroid shape

rare.symptomName: Mild respiratory stridor due to ectopic thyroid mass
searchTerms: mild breathing sounds due to neck mass

rare.symptomName: Congenital hypothyroidism-like symptoms despite normal labs (rare transient hypothyroidism)
searchTerms: symptoms like hypothyroidism but normal labs

rare.symptomName: Mild facial dysmorphism associated with syndromic thyroid malformations

laboratory: Normal serum TSH, free T4, and free T3 levels
Absence of thyroid autoantibodies or low titers
imaging: Ultrasound showing hypoplastic or ectopic thyroid tissue
Radionuclide thyroid scan demonstrating absent or ectopic uptake
genetic: Mutations in genes involved in thyroid development such as PAX8, TSHR, or FOXE1 without hypothyroidism phenotype

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated TSH and low thyroid hormone levels
Clinical signs of hypothyroidism such as lethargy and poor feeding

redFlags: Development of hypothyroid symptoms despite normal initial labs
Rapidly enlarging neck mass causing airway compromise
Failure to thrive or developmental delay
references: Orphanet: Congenital thyroid malformation without hypothyroidism, ORPHA:95718
